title: Tumor-derived antioxidants suppress immunity by depriving T cells of reactive oxygen species.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: No data files exist to open. I checked: Europe PMC (no PMCID, isOpenAccess=N, hasSuppl=N, hasData=N); science.org article page and the supplementary PDF URL (both HTTP 403, publisher paywall); PubMed's full XML record (no DataBank or AccessionNumber block, no PubMed Central link, only a 'subscription required' link); NCBI elink from PMID 42691162 (no GEO/SRA/BioProject/dbGaP links); GEO searched for Prdx1+immunoediting (0 hits), Wesolowski 2026 (0 hits), and all 2026 Prdx1 records (none match this study); PRIDE searched for 'tumor/tumour interstitial fluid', 'peroxiredoxin interstitial' and 'PRDX1' (12 PRDX1 projects, newest 2026-07, none from this lab or on interstitial fluid); ProteomeXchange keyword search 'interstitial fluid peroxiredoxin' (0 datasets); Zenodo searched for the authors and for PRDX1+interstitial (exactly 1 hit). That single Zenodo record (10.5281/zenodo.23164137, CC-BY-4.0, deposited 2026-10-05 by Wesolowski, Eil and Roychoudhuri) is one 96.1 kB PDF of a gel figure prepared as a reply to a Science eLetter, not a dataset. I confirmed its file list and size through the Zenodo API.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the study's content comes from the PubMed abstract plus university and trade press summaries (Cambridge, OHSU, EurekAlert, Inside Precision Medicine). From those: tumour interstitial fluid was collected from mouse tumours and from patient tumours, PRDX1 in tumour interstitial fluid was estimated at roughly 0.95 mg/mL, published human cancer cell line secretome data were reanalysed, and gene activity was examined across 'thousands of human tumours'. No sample counts, no table, and no methods section were retrievable; the full text and its data availability statement are paywalled.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL. There is no downloadable dataset. The article and its supplementary materials return HTTP 403 from science.org; the paper is not in PubMed Central (Science embargoes for 6-12 months, so a 2026-09-03 article is not yet deposited); PubMed lists no data bank accession; and GEO, SRA, PRIDE, ProteomeXchange, Zenodo and Dryad searches turned up nothing belonging to this study. The only public artefact is a 96 kB PDF of one gel figure on Zenodo.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: no data from this paper is publicly available, so no model could be trained or evaluated on it.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use tumour gene expression to predict how much antioxidant protein a tumour dumps into the fluid around its cells.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would have used each tumour's gene activity profile (how strongly each gene is switched on) as input, paired with a measurement of antioxidant enzyme protein in that same tumour's interstitial fluid - the liquid bathing the cells between blood vessels. Number of paired tumours: unknown, and almost certainly in the tens.
plain_idea.predict: The output would be the concentration or antioxidant activity of PRDX1 (peroxiredoxin 1, an enzyme that destroys hydrogen peroxide) in tumour interstitial fluid, measured by mass spectrometry or immunoassay on fluid squeezed or eluted from fresh tumour tissue.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: If gene expression predicted extracellular antioxidant load, the many thousands of already-sequenced tumours in public archives could be scored for this newly described 'redox checkpoint', telling immuno-oncology groups which patients might resist checkpoint immunotherapy. As it stands none of the needed paired measurements are public.

ml_idea: Considered and abandoned: predict tumour interstitial-fluid antioxidant load (PRDX1 protein or peroxide-clearing activity) from matched bulk tumour transcriptomes, then score public cohorts such as The Cancer Genome Atlas for a 'redox checkpoint' score and test it against immune checkpoint blockade response. This needs the paper's paired fluid-proteomics and transcriptome tables, none of which were deposited anywhere I could find.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: no data to size. Nothing was downloaded or timed beyond metadata requests.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Look for a deposited accession. One Europe PMC query plus GEO, PRIDE, ProteomeXchange and Zenodo searches (about ten minutes) showed there is none, which kills the project immediately.

verdict_reason: Part A1 fails outright. This is a paywalled Science mechanistic mouse-immunology paper with no PubMed Central deposit, no supplementary files reachable (HTTP 403), and no accession in GEO, SRA, PRIDE, ProteomeXchange, Zenodo or Dryad; the only public file is a 96 kB PDF figure answering an eLetter. Even if the supplement were opened later, the underlying measurements are mouse experiments and patient fluid samples numbering in the tens, which would also fail A5. Worth revisiting only if the authors deposit the interstitial-fluid proteomics, or after the Science embargo lifts and PubMed Central reveals a data availability statement with an accession.
